read.cue: two opponents are open at once — one on the doorstep, one back at the weak-side point; the doorstep man is the bigger threat

interaction.prompt: The puck's in your corner. Read the ice and drag YOURSELF (the defence) to where you're needed most.

feedback.right: Yes. Two of their players are open, but the one on the doorstep is the lethal one — a tap-in waiting to happen. Take the net-front first; the point shot is the lesser danger.
feedback.wrong: The weak-side point is open, but a point shot is far less dangerous than the man alone on the doorstep. Always take the highest-danger threat — the net-front — first.

tip: When two men are open, cover the most dangerous one first: the doorstep beats the point every time.
why: Defensive-zone coverage is triage. With two threats open, the net-front man scores the easy goal, so he gets covered before the lower-danger point.
